# Core/Rust convergence: exact f654 and public e0 evidence

This package preserves the actual local and public executions of the bounded
Core/Rust convergence candidate, together with its source reconstruction,
original failed controls, independent review, and the original official CI
failure. It does not convert a later repair or a historical qualification into
an execution on a different commit.

## Source identities

| Role | Commit | Tree |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing PR405 parent | `192d2cbba7e49bde3b03af73685ecf96f6fb1b05` | `30c20454c3e08990a7995306f31ff21acad182f4` |
| Frozen local convergence | `f6540186aa34c991b2082d59cd998b857f78ced4` | `7adcc2a0333b48374b4add2d8132d1998c5cc48c` |
| Public PR410 convergence | `e0b9012a249167b5bc5b0f3bd243899344621080` | `7adcc2a0333b48374b4add2d8132d1998c5cc48c` |

The two convergence commits have the same tree and the same PR405 parent, but
their commit identities and actual executions remain separate. The source
export retains 32 exact UTF-8 files, Git modes and blob IDs, a full-index patch,
and an independently reconstructed tree. The export's original
`qualification_running` status is a historical snapshot and is not rewritten.
Later actual execution receipts carry their own outcomes.

## What changed

The integration preserves PR405's existing opcode catalog, schema registry,
Core checker, runtime, Machine, sealed-memfd differential custody, immutable
argument snapshot, nested returned-field origins, and bounded empty-record
walk. It adds the already qualified finite raw Rust Copy-record frontpass to
that newer implementation, restoring one route into the existing primitive
Core and Machine without a second evaluator or a production-authority switch.

The raw candidate accepts only explicit monomorphic acyclic Copy records,
including nested and empty records. Nominal types, zero-width bindings and
source-derived export eligibility are checked before erasure. Unsupported
forms anywhere in the module fail closed. This is not general raw composite
support. The direct raw CLI's executable hash checks are distinct from the
sealed custody of the production differential wrapper.

The composite v4 adapter accepts the historical string origin only when it
names the original primitive borrowed formal with sufficient permission; it
then uses the newer existing origin resolver. The newer field-origin grammar
is retained. ELF driver contexts restore real selected-executable/alias
identity and exception cleanup checks while preserving current dispatcher and
bound-IR behavior. The separate P3 patch reads and rechecks the admitted
canonical C source and refuses a direct leaf source symlink; it preserves the
stronger existing migration IR and captured-stdin publication behavior.

## Actual required execution scopes

| Gate | Actual local f654 | Actual public e0 | Retained scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rust crate | 96 tests / 19 harnesses, pass | 96 tests / 19 harnesses, pass | Full existing crate plus raw frontpass tests |
| Raw record collector | 9 methods, pass | 9 methods, pass | 13 exact normalizations, 43 executions, 47 refusals; 103 native processes per run |
| Bound-v4 API collector | 8 methods, pass | 8 methods, pass | 155 positive observations, 37 refusals, 72 legacy report comparisons per run |
| Historical composite-origin collector | 13 methods, pass | 13 methods, pass | 153 Rust observations, 4 raw refusals, 31 native calls per run |
| Current field-origin and mixed-origin selection | 16 methods, pass | 16 methods, pass | 239 Rust observations, 11 raw refusals, 4 source cases; 54 oracle native rows plus 6 negative controls per run |
| Shared guards | 70 methods, pass | 70 methods, pass | Actual protocol, linker, registry and workflow guards |
| Required migration selection | 177 methods / 27 modules, pass | 177 methods / 27 modules, pass | P3 owner retained both exact-head runs |
| Canonical safety selection | Not repeated on f654 | 340 actual methods, pass in this workspace | Every expected method has one ordinary passing event; source, tools and external inputs stable |

These scopes overlap. Their counts must not be added into a count of distinct
coverage. The safety contract retains all 277 PR405 selectors and all 126 prior
raw-record selectors, including the 46 old selectors absent from PR405, then
adds current field-origin, mixed-origin and P3 obligations for exactly 340
selectors and 36 capabilities. Discovery alone is not execution; this package
also retains the actual 340-method event multiset and full logs.

The public Rust binary has SHA256
`090ea31c9631aae744d8a72b3eb1f753bba1a36edf887d564145546865761362`
and size 4,204,464 bytes. Executed binaries, native artifacts and original
per-gate build/process records are included. The full source identity checks
cover the materialized tracked tree; that coverage is not full-project test
coverage.

## Original official CI failure remains a failure

On public e0, official source/application run `41055139018`, job
`124060656375`, completed the safety selection with **339 ordinary passes and
one failed subtest**. The original artifact ZIP, its content, and the job log
are retained. The failure was the `fork_and_stall` case of the native child
limit test: the existing 0.2-second observation ended as a timeout while the
assertion required actual SIGSYS. The original record alone does not determine
how startup, scheduling, loading and evaluation divided that elapsed time.

The local public e0 run passed all 340 methods in its recorded environment.
That success does not erase the official failure or qualify the skipped later
official steps. A separately preserved controlled-startup experiment and a
later two-file test-fixture repair have separate source identities and belong
to the guard-fix evidence package, not this e0 execution corpus.

The separate actual generic Rust LLD fixture red is also preserved. It is a
different test-fixture defect: a bound-IR fixture supplied a generic linker
spelling directly to a production guard requiring an ELF driver. It is not
the cause of the official native-child timeout.

## Provenance and restoration

The producer scripts, selected environments, source before/after inventories,
tool versions and hashes, exact outputs, source exports, publication receipts,
initial development failures, corrections, and final independent e0 review
are included unchanged. The independent reviewer audited original contents
without adding native executions. Reviewer-only harness/metadata failures and
their corrections remain in that review archive.

The NDU profiles use retained original executables from the official public147
artifact. Their original compiler versions, build costs, source pins and
denied authority remain unchanged; these are new runtime observations using
retained artifacts, not newly measured builds. The package includes their
restoration receipt, exact identity/handshake outputs and derived transport
manifests. The transport change is the local executable path only.

The original ZIP is recoverable from the immutable public evidence commit
`156dbba842999b1165e0964146decf58b3fc64a7` at
`evidence/hia_core_closure_20261029/hosted-147d39-evidence/full-release/`.
Its retained publication map and 89-part offset manifest specify all bytes;
the original size is 370,966,739 bytes and SHA256 is
`515b2166e3b47c0b51b46421f67531eb053ac21266a8202cba8ba0ba8dc95c6c`.
The package includes the root's actual remote full-stream reconstruction
receipt. Huge toolchain installations and this already published whole ZIP
are not duplicated here.

## Limits

Python remains the production admission/execution authority. No optimization
policy or production switch is changed. These finite qualification profiles
do not establish general memory/provenance, arbitrary recursive ADTs, complete
initialization/escaping/external lifetimes, callbacks/reentrancy/threads,
asynchronous cleanup, all historical migration configurations, independent
agent efficiency, representative throughput/tail latency, physical devices,
whole-language soundness or backend refinement. Logical resource ledgers and
address-space limits are not RSS measurements. The broad P0–P7 obligations
remain open.

The archive manifest and full-stream readback bind every included file's
path, mode, bytes, SHA256 and Git blob ID. Archive-part identities describe
transport only and do not add execution or qualification claims.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Freeze completed convergence evidence; never execute or rewrite a corpus."""
from hashlib import sha1, sha256
import io
import json
import lzma
from pathlib import Path
import stat
import tarfile
import time

WORKSPACE = Path('/workspace/scratch/b484d4086829')
OUTPUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ARCHIVE = OUTPUT / 'core-rust-convergence-f654-e0.tar.xz'
REPOSITORY_PREFIX = 'evidence/hia_core_closure_20261029/integration-convergence-e0-evidence'
ROOTS = [
    'core-rust-integration-validation', 'core-rust-public-validation',
    'core-rust-public-safety340', 'integration-405-147-20261030',
    'integration-405-p3-validation', 'public-405-p3-validation',
    'integration-ci-e0b9012-failure', 'ndu-restoration-20261030',
]
FILES = [
    'integration-convergence-e0-evidence/README.md',
    'integration-convergence-e0-evidence/package.py',
    'integration-convergence-e0-evidence/restore.py',
    'integration-405-independent-review/ndu-147-reuse-locator.json',
    'integration-405-independent-review/integration-e0-publication-files.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/integration-f654-source-export.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/integration-f654-source-publication.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/integration-pr-receipt.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/integration-pr-initial-body.md',
    'progress-publication-20261029/integration-source-application-job-124060656375.log',
    'progress-publication-20261029/integration-source-application-ci-failure-jobs.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/qemu-restoration-20261030.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/z3-restoration-20261030.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/llvm20-restoration-publication.json',
    'llvm-restoration-20261029-evening/summary.json',
    'llvm-restoration-20261029-evening/publication-metadata.json',
    'llvm-restoration-20261029-evening/metadata-archive-receipt.json',
    'llvm-restoration-20261029-evening/llvm20-env.sh',
    'hosted-147d39-evidence/full-release/publication-metadata.json',
    'hosted-147d39-evidence/full-release/raw-parts.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/full147-final-tree-readback.json',
    'progress-publication-20261029/full147-actual-remote-stream-readback.json',
    'toolchains/retained-ndu-147/recursive/transport-identity.json',
    'toolchains/retained-ndu-147/finite/transport-identity.json',
    'toolchains/retained-ndu-147/stream/transport-identity.json',
    'integration-convergence-e0-evidence/runtime-restoration-links.json',
]


def identity(path):
    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
        raise ValueError('regular immutable input required: ' + str(path))
    size = path.stat().st_size
    digest, blob = sha256(), sha1(b'blob ' + str(size).encode() + b'\0')
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        while raw := stream.read(1024 * 1024):
            digest.update(raw)
            blob.update(raw)
    return {'bytes': size, 'sha256': digest.hexdigest(), 'git_blob': blob.hexdigest(),
            'mode': oct(stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode))}


def save(name, document):
    path = OUTPUT / name
    if path.exists():
        raise ValueError('never overwrite a packaging record: ' + str(path))
    path.write_text(json.dumps(document, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n')
    return path


def main():
    if ARCHIVE.exists():
        raise ValueError('never overwrite an evidence archive')
    clock = time.monotonic()
    peer_map = json.loads((WORKSPACE / 'integration-405-independent-review/integration-e0-publication-files.json').read_text())
    peer_archive = peer_map['archive']
    assert peer_archive['sha256'] == '2338edcc21bbb3f4b757f749b20ce5c4c5672b17e3375ebe0eb99dd3ede3844d'
    for row in peer_map['files']:
        actual = identity(Path(row['path']))
        assert all(actual[key] == row[key] for key in ('bytes', 'sha256', 'git_blob'))
    paths = {WORKSPACE / name for name in FILES}
    paths.update(Path(row['path']) for row in peer_map['files'])
    for root in ROOTS:
        paths.update(path for path in (WORKSPACE / root).rglob('*')
                     if path.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in path.parts)
    before = {str(path.relative_to(WORKSPACE)): identity(path) for path in sorted(paths)}
    manifest = {'schema': 'hepta.convergence-e0-evidence-manifest.v1',
                'local_head': 'f6540186aa34c991b2082d59cd998b857f78ced4',
                'public_head': 'e0b9012a249167b5bc5b0f3bd243899344621080',
                'shared_tree': '7adcc2a0333b48374b4add2d8132d1998c5cc48c',
                'inputs': before, 'input_count': len(before),
                'input_bytes': sum(row['bytes'] for row in before.values()),
                'excluded_reproducible_import_caches': ['__pycache__'],
                'official_e0_safety_outcome': {'ordinary_passes': 339, 'failed_subtests': 1},
                'local_public_e0_safety_outcome': {'ordinary_passes': 340, 'failed_subtests': 0},
                'historical_failed_controls_retained': True,
                'new_native_executions_by_packaging': 0,
                'giant_toolchain_installations_or_original_ndu_zip_duplicated': False,
                'later_guard_fix_or_p0_executions_relabelled': False}
    manifest_path = save('archive-manifest.json', manifest)
    archive_inputs = dict(before)
    manifest_name = str(manifest_path.relative_to(WORKSPACE))
    archive_inputs[manifest_name] = identity(manifest_path)
    print(json.dumps({'phase': 'archive', 'members': len(archive_inputs),
                      'input_bytes': manifest['input_bytes']}), flush=True)
    with tarfile.open(ARCHIVE, 'w:xz', preset=9, format=tarfile.PAX_FORMAT) as archive:
        for name, expected in sorted(archive_inputs.items()):
            path = WORKSPACE / name
            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
            info.size, info.mode, info.mtime = expected['bytes'], int(expected['mode'], 8), 0
            info.uid = info.gid = 0
            info.uname = info.gname = ''
            with path.open('rb') as stream:
                archive.addfile(info, stream)
    print(json.dumps({'phase': 'readback', 'compressed_bytes': ARCHIVE.stat().st_size}), flush=True)
    seen = []
    with tarfile.open(ARCHIVE, 'r:xz') as archive:
        for member in archive:
            assert member.isfile() and member.name in archive_inputs and member.name not in seen
            expected = archive_inputs[member.name]
            assert member.size == expected['bytes'] and member.mode == int(expected['mode'], 8)
            digest, blob = sha256(), sha1(b'blob ' + str(member.size).encode() + b'\0')
            with archive.extractfile(member) as stream:
                while raw := stream.read(1024 * 1024):
                    digest.update(raw)
                    blob.update(raw)
            assert digest.hexdigest() == expected['sha256'] and blob.hexdigest() == expected['git_blob']
            seen.append(member.name)
    assert set(seen) == set(archive_inputs)
    # Consume the compression stream through EOF, including its trailing check.
    expanded = 0
    with lzma.open(ARCHIVE, 'rb') as stream:
        while raw := stream.read(1024 * 1024):
            expanded += len(raw)
    after = {name: identity(WORKSPACE / name) for name in before}
    assert before == after
    archive_identity = identity(ARCHIVE)
    parts = []
    offset = 0
    digest = sha256()
    blob = sha1(b'blob ' + str(archive_identity['bytes']).encode() + b'\0')
    with ARCHIVE.open('rb') as stream:
        while raw := stream.read(4 * 1024 * 1024):
            name = ARCHIVE.name + '.part' + str(len(parts) + 1).zfill(3)
            parts.append({'name': name, 'repository_path': REPOSITORY_PREFIX + '/' + name,
                          'local_archive': str(ARCHIVE), 'offset': offset, 'bytes': len(raw),
                          'sha256': sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
                          'git_blob': sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(raw)).encode() + b'\0' + raw).hexdigest(),
                          'mode': '100644'})
            digest.update(raw)
            blob.update(raw)
            offset += len(raw)
    assert offset == archive_identity['bytes']
    assert digest.hexdigest() == archive_identity['sha256'] and blob.hexdigest() == archive_identity['git_blob']
    receipt = {'schema': 'hepta.convergence-e0-archive-readback.v1',
               'archive': {'path': str(ARCHIVE), **archive_identity},
               'member_count': len(seen), 'all_paths_modes_sizes_sha256_git_blobs_match': True,
               'full_xz_stream_eof_and_check_consumed': True, 'uncompressed_tar_bytes': expanded,
               'original_inputs_unchanged': before == after, 'original_input_count': len(before),
               'ordered_parts_cover_archive_exactly': True, 'part_count': len(parts),
               'wall_seconds': time.monotonic() - clock, 'new_native_or_test_executions': 0}
    receipt_path = save('archive-readback.json', receipt)
    part_path = save('archive-parts.json', {'schema': 'hepta.evidence-archive-offset-parts.v1',
        'archive': {'path': str(ARCHIVE), **archive_identity}, 'chunk_bytes': 4 * 1024 * 1024,
        'parts': parts, 'part_count': len(parts), 'physical_part_files_created': False,
        'ordered_ranges_cover_original_exactly': True,
        'publication_method': 'Read each exact offset/length from local_archive; uploaded part bytes must match both digests. Restore expects the downloaded named part files.'})
    files = []
    for path in (OUTPUT / 'README.md', OUTPUT / 'package.py', OUTPUT / 'restore.py', OUTPUT / 'runtime-restoration-links.json',
                 manifest_path, receipt_path, part_path):
        files.append({'local_path': str(path), 'repository_path': REPOSITORY_PREFIX + '/' + path.name,
                      **identity(path), 'mode': '100755' if path.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else '100644'})
    publication = {'schema': 'hepta.convergence-e0-publication.v1',
                   'source_head': manifest['public_head'], 'historical_local_head': manifest['local_head'],
                   'source_tree': manifest['shared_tree'], 'payload_files': files,
                   'archive_parts': parts, 'archive': {'path': str(ARCHIVE), **archive_identity},
                   'also_publish_this_map': True,
                   'map_repository_path': REPOSITORY_PREFIX + '/publication-files.json',
                   'no_remote_writes_by_this_agent': True,
                   'remote_publication_verified_by_packager': False,
                   'qualification_scope': 'Actual f654/public e0 local corpus only; original official e0 safety failure retained; later fixes separate.'}
    publication_path = save('publication-files.json', publication)
    print(json.dumps({'complete': True, 'archive_bytes': archive_identity['bytes'],
                      'archive_sha256': archive_identity['sha256'], 'members': len(seen),
                      'parts': len(parts), 'manifest_sha256': identity(publication_path)['sha256']}), flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reassemble downloaded exact archive parts without extracting the archive."""
import argparse
from hashlib import sha1, sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--manifest', type=Path, default=Path('archive-parts.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--parts-directory', type=Path, default=Path('.'))
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    options = parser.parse_args()
    document = json.loads(options.manifest.read_text())
    expected = document['archive']
    if options.output.exists():
        raise ValueError('output already exists; preserve previous restorations')
    digest, blob = sha256(), sha1(b'blob ' + str(expected['bytes']).encode() + b'\0')
    offset = 0
    with options.output.open('xb') as output:
        for row in document['parts']:
            if row['offset'] != offset or Path(row['name']).name != row['name']:
                raise ValueError('invalid ordered part path or offset')
            raw = (options.parts_directory / row['name']).read_bytes()
            if len(raw) != row['bytes'] or sha256(raw).hexdigest() != row['sha256']:
                raise ValueError('part size or SHA256 mismatch: ' + row['name'])
            if sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(raw)).encode() + b'\0' + raw).hexdigest() != row['git_blob']:
                raise ValueError('part Git blob mismatch: ' + row['name'])
            output.write(raw)
            digest.update(raw)
            blob.update(raw)
            offset += len(raw)
    if (offset != expected['bytes'] or digest.hexdigest() != expected['sha256']
            or blob.hexdigest() != expected['git_blob']):
        raise ValueError('complete reconstructed archive identity mismatch; partial output retained')
    print(json.dumps({'output': str(options.output), 'bytes': offset,
                      'sha256': digest.hexdigest(), 'git_blob': blob.hexdigest(), 'ok': True}))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

controlled validation, and new executions on its exact public commit. It
preserves the original failed outcomes and keeps every source identity
separate.

## Native child startup budget

Original official e0 source/application run `41055139018`, job
`124060656375`, ran 340 selected methods with 339 ordinary passes and one
failed subtest. `fork_and_stall` timed out under its 0.2-second total budget
before the test observed its required SIGSYS result. The original CI record
does not isolate exactly how that elapsed time was divided among startup,
scheduling, loading and evaluation.

A separate real controlled experiment added a 0.35-second startup delay only
to the two fork worker paths, before the original worker and syscall filter.
It did not replace process status, native execution, filtering or assertions.
On the unchanged e0 source, the actual child exit codes were
`[-9, -31, -9]`: the first fork test failed by timing out before reaching the
original worker; the second fork test reached the forbidden syscall and died
with SIGSYS; the ordinary stall still timed out. This expected reproduction
remains a failed test, not a passing qualification.

The repair gives both fork cases the existing 3-second startup allowance.
The non-forking stall retains its 0.2-second deadline. Both fork assertions
still require SIGSYS(-31), and the actual marker/cleanup assertions remain.
With the same controlled delay, the local repair and the public repair each
actually produced `[-31, -31, -9]`, three absent-marker observations, and an
unchanged empty cleanup state. All original/delayed worker source, native C
and ELF bytes, child argv/exit codes, timings, marker observations and logs
are retained.

The repair makes that fixture enter the existing `elf_linker_driver` context

def identity(path):
    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
        raise ValueError('regular immutable input required: ' + str(path))
    size = path.stat().st_size
    digest, blob = sha256(), sha1(b'blob ' + str(size).encode() + b'\0')
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        while raw := stream.read(1024 * 1024):
            digest.update(raw)
            blob.update(raw)
    return {'bytes': size, 'sha256': digest.hexdigest(), 'git_blob': blob.hexdigest(),
            'mode': oct(stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode))}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reassemble downloaded exact archive parts without extracting the archive."""
import argparse
from hashlib import sha1, sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--manifest', type=Path, default=Path('archive-parts.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--parts-directory', type=Path, default=Path('.'))
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    options = parser.parse_args()
    document = json.loads(options.manifest.read_text())
    expected = document['archive']
    if options.output.exists():
        raise ValueError('output already exists; preserve previous restorations')
    digest, blob = sha256(), sha1(b'blob ' + str(expected['bytes']).encode() + b'\0')
    offset = 0
    with options.output.open('xb') as output:
        for row in document['parts']:
            if row['offset'] != offset or Path(row['name']).name != row['name']:
                raise ValueError('invalid ordered part path or offset')
            raw = (options.parts_directory / row['name']).read_bytes()
            if len(raw) != row['bytes'] or sha256(raw).hexdigest() != row['sha256']:
                raise ValueError('part size or SHA256 mismatch: ' + row['name'])
            if sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(raw)).encode() + b'\0' + raw).hexdigest() != row['git_blob']:
                raise ValueError('part Git blob mismatch: ' + row['name'])
            output.write(raw)
            digest.update(raw)
            blob.update(raw)
            offset += len(raw)
    if (offset != expected['bytes'] or digest.hexdigest() != expected['sha256']
            or blob.hexdigest() != expected['git_blob']):
        raise ValueError('complete reconstructed archive identity mismatch; partial output retained')
    print(json.dumps({'output': str(options.output), 'bytes': offset,
                      'sha256': digest.hexdigest(), 'git_blob': blob.hexdigest(), 'ok': True}))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

from hashlib import sha1, sha256
import json
import lzma
from pathlib import Path
import re
import stat
import tarfile

ROOT = Path('/workspace/scratch/b484d4086829')
OUTPUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'frozen-packages-readback.json'
PACKAGES = [
    ('integration-convergence-e0-evidence',
     'af42f862078debb66f7dfdcbb8e390eec2793facdd8dfb87e176b9ec5a7da5c3',
     'integration-405-independent-review/integration-e0-independent-review.tar.gz',
     '2338edcc21bbb3f4b757f749b20ce5c4c5672b17e3375ebe0eb99dd3ede3844d'),
    ('guard-fix-evidence',
     '440cf608255a741c34c7d8581ada2f458fe20802882bd8bbad4a4b3b5f28a5f6',
     'guard-fix-independent-review/guard-fix-independent-review-40ae.tar.gz',
     'd6da0b8d6ab3063fbef51e1cb75d19f3b3201ec8cf1e4f317b614173992fd961'),
]
SIGNED_URL = re.compile(rb'https?://[^\s<>"\']*[?&](?:sig|signature|token|access_token|x-amz-signature)=', re.I)


def identity(path: Path):
    assert path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink(), str(path)
    size = path.stat().st_size
    h, git = sha256(), sha1(b'blob ' + str(size).encode() + b'\0')
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
            h.update(chunk)
            git.update(chunk)
    return {'bytes': size, 'sha256': h.hexdigest(), 'git_blob': git.hexdigest(),
            'mode': oct(stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode))}


def assert_identity(actual, expected, context):
    assert all(actual[k] == expected[k] for k in ('bytes', 'sha256', 'git_blob')), context


def main():
    assert not OUTPUT.exists(), 'Never overwrite a readback receipt'
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    results = []
    for folder, archive_digest, peer_name, peer_digest in PACKAGES:
        directory = ROOT / folder
        map_path = directory / 'publication-files.json'
        publication = json.loads(map_path.read_text())
        archive_path = Path(publication['archive']['path'])
        assert publication['archive']['sha256'] == archive_digest
        assert_identity(identity(archive_path), publication['archive'], 'whole archive')
        manifest_path = directory / 'archive-manifest.json'
        manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
        original = manifest['inputs']
        assert len(original) == manifest['input_count']
        assert sum(v['bytes'] for v in original.values()) == manifest['input_bytes']
        assert all('private-transport' not in name and '__pycache__' not in name for name in original)
        assert all(not name.endswith('/official-full-release-147d39.zip') for name in original)
        assert original[peer_name]['sha256'] == peer_digest
        assert sum(name == peer_name for name in original) == 1

        # Check persistence of every original input without changing it.
        for name, expected in original.items():
            actual = identity(ROOT / name)
            assert actual == expected, 'persisted original: ' + name
        expected_members = dict(original)
        expected_members[str(manifest_path.relative_to(ROOT))] = identity(manifest_path)
        seen = set()
        signed_url_findings = []
        with tarfile.open(archive_path, 'r:xz') as archive:
            for member in archive:
                assert member.isfile() and member.name not in seen
                assert member.name in expected_members, member.name
                expected = expected_members[member.name]
                assert member.size == expected['bytes'] and member.mode == int(expected['mode'], 8)
                h, git = sha256(), sha1(b'blob ' + str(member.size).encode() + b'\0')
                carry = b''
                with archive.extractfile(member) as stream:
                    for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
                        h.update(chunk)
                        git.update(chunk)
                        if SIGNED_URL.search(carry + chunk):
                            signed_url_findings.append(member.name)
                        carry = (carry + chunk)[-8192:]
                assert h.hexdigest() == expected['sha256'] and git.hexdigest() == expected['git_blob']
                seen.add(member.name)
        assert seen == set(expected_members)

                offset += len(raw)
            assert stream.read(1) == b''
        assert offset == publication['archive']['bytes']
        for entry in publication['payload_files']:
            assert_identity(identity(Path(entry['local_path'])), entry, entry['local_path'])
        results.append({'directory': folder, 'source_head': publication['source_head'],

# Returned byte calls compose with local Views in the existing v8 route

## Frozen source and exact scope

The final local candidate is `0d077885cc4be0b8ee96a012d7d6d2e51d1d2ace`, tree
`88478a74708cf63edf7f9304c0b4ceb820b04d01`, following local candidate
`31736998decf7fe952617fd219130ee3a5048a9e`. Its public source base is
`b121c9b4a57a8a58e53360d1d67387d953348f57`. That base includes the two independent
CI fixture corrections; their source and earlier observations are not relabeled
as part of this implementation. Source publication and a later public-head
execution, when available, require separate mappings and observations.

Production changes are confined to `hepta/hia_program_source.py`. The other
nine paths contain the example, nine regression methods, existing safety and
critical/workflow registrations, and documentation. There is no new language
schema, source option, route, checker, evaluator, Machine or native backend.
Python remains the production admission authority and optimization remains
`no_change`.

## Actual rejected composition and implementation

The unchanged source checker requires an explicit outer borrow in a stored
reference field: `View {data: read shared(read data), tag: 7}`. Four such source
programs passed source checking and the existing ResourceIR verification on
pristine public `e0b9012a249167b5bc5b0f3bd243899344621080`. Its HIA source adapter
then rejected all four at `borrow and assignment places must be local records
or fields`. The actual source, ResourceIR documents and errors are retained in
`explicit-e0-preconditions/`. This establishes a concrete boundary between
already legal source/resource semantics and the old executable-source adapter.

The initial four probes omitted that outer `read` or `mut`, following a
historical negative fixture. Those programs failed source checking with
`E_BORROW_MODE`; they were not legal counterexamples to the HIA adapter. Their
original results remain in `pristine-e0-preconditions/`. The corrected probes
have separate source hashes and observations. The initial syntax error was
not repaired by weakening the source checker.

The existing explicit `core_schema=hepta.hia.program.v8` route now accepts a
stored call result with these limits:

- Each local View record has one `[u8]` reference field and up to four scalar
  labels, admitted by the existing source checker and ResourceIR rules.
- The called helper returns a borrowed `[u8]` slice and has exactly one borrowed
  byte-slice or byte-buffer formal. Formal, result and stored field have the
  same `read` or `mut` permission. Other formals are ordinary scalar values.
- The actual origin is a direct named byte owner, borrowed parameter or field
  of an available ordinary owner record. A nested returned-call argument,
  local-View origin, aggregate borrowed formal or permission conversion is
  outside this increment.
- View parameters, View returns, nested View records, multiple stored loans,
  named lifetime escape, and a standalone stored returned slice remain refused.
  Default v1 still refuses the new returned-call construction. Readless or
  mutless stored fields remain source-checker errors.

The adapter selects its existing v8 `call()` implementation. That implementation
already produces the argument parent loan and returned child loan. The new
work preserves the parent value through View construction, local binding,
shared Copy and exclusive move. `_State.prune` retains the transitive
`borrow_parents` dependencies, so the existing block builder includes the
hidden capability in ordinary CFG interfaces. Edges also require the same
producer parent binding. This is producer bookkeeping; the primitive Core
verifier independently checks the emitted capabilities and edges.

Shared copies alias the same obligation. An inner copy cannot end a parent or
child still held by an outer copy. The final lexical alias ends the child
before its argument parent. Exclusive View moves invalidate the old binding,
and explicit `drop(move view)` releases both capabilities in that order.
Exclusive scope exit and early return do not invent a destructor. The example
contains both valid early-return and normal-return paths that explicitly drop
the exclusive View before the caller accesses and drops the owner.

hidden argument parent when local temporaries are pruned or passed through CFG

It stopped before any LLVM compile or call. The original collector and traceback remain. Completion reused the six original Rust records and executed only the outstanding LLVM phase.
